requirements_artifact.problem_statement: Build a small, private, daily energy-markets newsletter. A deterministic pipeline reads a curated list of reputable, mostly tier-1 sources once a day (official agencies and regulators, major news organizations with corrections policies, specialist carbon and energy press), tags and groups the stories, and publishes a digest. A Claude scheduled task on the owner's subscription reads that digest, tracks trends (ideas that multiple companies are pushing, with their trajectory), and writes a condensed newsletter plus a 'What this means for energy traders' analysis. A validator checks both before they appear on a web page with tabs for crude oil, natural gas, refined products and carbon credits. v1 is news-only; price data is deferred.
in_scope: Curated reputable source registry with tiers, types and terms status
Deterministic commodity, topic and organization tagging
Digest snapshot and compact Markdown digest for the author
Trend ledger with company verification, status, trajectory and hotness
Daily newsletter and trader analysis written by a Claude scheduled task
Validator gate with reject and warn rules
Web page: Newsletter, Analysis, Trends, All and four commodity tabs
Carbon Credits as a v1 commodity
Custom domain, noindex and private-preview disclaimer
out_of_scope: Price data, benchmark moves and price effects (deferred, FR-8)
Price forecasts, trade ideas or investment advice
Any LLM API usage or API keys
Automated collection or AI summarization of CDR.fyi or other REFERENCE_ONLY sources
Email delivery and user accounts (growth path)
True access control in v1 (GitHub Pages is public; noindex only)

assumptions.statement: v1 commodities are Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refined Products and Carbon Credits.
Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, S&P Global Platts and Argus require licenses and stay BLOCKED; tier-1 coverage comes from official publishers and outlets with public feeds.

Company press-release wires (e.g. PR Newswire Energy) are tier-2 NEWSROOM sources: good evidence of what a company is pushing, not independent confirmation. A CONFIRMED trend needs 2+ companies but not an independent source; the analysis must say when a trend rests only on company releases.
The readership is the owner and a friend; the page is public-but-unlisted (noindex), prefaced as unverified. If it grows, add access control and review each source's terms for wider distribution.

Claude scheduled tasks count against the owner's plan usage; one bounded run per day is expected to fit. If a run fails on usage limits, the site shows the data-only synopsis and the previous newsletter.

Several reputable feeds (The Guardian, BBC, Financial Times, CNBC, OPEC, UNFCCC) could not be verified from the planning environment; they ship enabled or pending per the registry and the first run report (AC-1.4) confirms them from the GitHub runner.
The existing stack is reused: Python 3.12, SQLite, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages; the owner buys a domain and points it at Pages.

constraints.scale: About 25-35 enabled sources, roughly 150-400 new articles per day, one private web page for a handful of readers, with room to grow.
constraints.latency: Daily scan completes in under 15 minutes; the newsletter is live by about 08:00 America/Chicago; the page is interactive in under 2 s.
constraints.cost: No API spend; free CI and hosting; existing Claude subscription; optional domain (roughly the price of a domain registration per year).
constraints.team_size: One developer plus the scheduled Claude task.
constraints.existing_stack: Python 3.12, SQLite, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, Claude scheduled tasks with the GitHub connector.
constraints.compliance: Reputable sources only; honour robots.txt and terms; excerpts and links only; no scraping or AI use of CDR.fyi data without a license; unverified, not-investment-advice disclaimer; noindex.

requirements.statement: Maintain a source registry (config file). Every source declares id, name, url, tier, source_type, commodities, access_method (RSS | HTML_LIST), tos_status (ALLOWED | HEADLINE_ONLY | REFERENCE_ONLY | BLOCKED | UNVERIFIED), terms_note and enabled. Tier 1 = official or primary publishers (government agencies, regulators, intergovernmental bodies) and news organizations with a public editorial and corrections policy; tier 2 = specialist trade press and company press-release wires; tier 3 = aggregators and commentary, disabled by default. source_type is OFFICIAL | PRESS | TRADE | NEWSROOM | AGGREGATOR.

acceptance_criteria.given: a source whose tos_status is BLOCKED, UNVERIFIED or REFERENCE_ONLY
acceptance_criteria.then: no HTTP request is made to it and the run report lists it as SKIPPED with its tos_status

acceptance_criteria.given: a registry entry with a duplicate id, a tier outside 1-3, or an unknown source_type
acceptance_criteria.then: loading fails with a validation error naming the entry and no scan starts

acceptance_criteria.given: a tier-3 AGGREGATOR entry with enabled omitted
acceptance_criteria.then: it is treated as disabled

acceptance_criteria.given: the first successful daily run
acceptance_criteria.then: it lists every enabled source with OK, NOT_MODIFIED, FAILED or ROBOTS_DISALLOWED so the owner can confirm which reputable feeds work from the runner

requirements.rationale: Reputable, well-checked sources are the product. Tier and type drive weighting, and terms status decides what the scanner may touch.

requirements.statement: Once per day, scan enabled sources in tier order, honouring robots.txt and conditional GET, and store only items not already seen after URL canonicalisation. RSS sources are parsed as feeds; official sources without RSS use an HTML_LIST adapter configured with CSS selectors for item link, title and date.

acceptance_criteria.given: an item whose URL differs from a stored item only by utm_* parameters or a trailing slash
acceptance_criteria.then: it is recognised as a duplicate and not stored again

acceptance_criteria.given: one source times out or returns HTTP 5xx
acceptance_criteria.then: that source is recorded FAILED with the reason, every other source is still scanned, and the run completes

acceptance_criteria.given: a source has FAILED on 3 consecutive daily runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the source carries a STALE_SOURCE flag

acceptance_criteria.given: robots.txt disallows the listing or article path
acceptance_criteria.then: it is not fetched and is recorded ROBOTS_DISALLOWED

acceptance_criteria.given: an HTML_LIST source (e.g. ICAP news) whose page yields items with title, link and date via the configured selectors
acceptance_criteria.then: each item becomes a stored article exactly as an RSS item would; if the selectors match nothing the source is FAILED with reason SELECTOR_NO_MATCH

requirements.statement: Read each new item: title, canonical url, outlet, published_at (UTC) and a persisted excerpt of at most 300 characters. HEADLINE_ONLY sources use only the listing or feed title and summary; ALLOWED sources may fetch the article body transiently for tagging and figure extraction.

acceptance_criteria.given: an article with no parseable publish timestamp
acceptance_criteria.then: it is marked UNDATED and excluded from the digest, trends and newsletter candidates

acceptance_criteria.given: a HEADLINE_ONLY source
acceptance_criteria.when: one of its items is read
acceptance_criteria.then: the article page is never requested by the pipeline

acceptance_criteria.given: an article published '2026-09-09 10:35 EDT'
acceptance_criteria.then: published_at is stored as 2026-09-09T14:35:00Z

requirements.statement: Tag every article deterministically (no LLM API): one or more commodities from CRUDE_OIL, NATURAL_GAS, REFINED_PRODUCTS, CARBON_CREDITS; one topic from the closed topic list; and the organizations it names, matched against a maintained organizations file (name, aliases, org_type COMPANY | GOVERNMENT | AGENCY | INTERGOVERNMENTAL).

acceptance_criteria.given: the headline 'Venture Global and Cheniere expand US LNG export capacity'
acceptance_criteria.then: commodities include NATURAL_GAS and organizations include Venture Global and Cheniere Energy (via alias 'Cheniere'), both COMPANY

acceptance_criteria.given: an article with no commodity keyword matches
acceptance_criteria.then: it is marked NOT_RELEVANT and excluded from all outputs

acceptance_criteria.given: the headline 'EU carbon allowances slide after Commission proposes changes to EU ETS auctions'
acceptance_criteria.then: its commodities are exactly CARBON_CREDITS and organizations include European Commission as GOVERNMENT

requirements.statement: Group articles from different outlets that report the same event into a story cluster with distinct_source_count, best source tier, organizations (union) and first_published_at.

acceptance_criteria.given: 4 articles from 4 sources about the same EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report within 24 h
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one cluster is formed with distinct_source_count = 4

acceptance_criteria.given: 3 articles from one source about one event
acceptance_criteria.then: they share one cluster and the source counts once

acceptance_criteria.given: two OPEC+ meeting articles more than 72 h apart
acceptance_criteria.then: they form two clusters

acceptance_criteria.given: identical inputs and configuration
acceptance_criteria.then: membership is identical

requirements.statement: Extract key reported figures verbatim (exact quoted span, unit as written, source url) from text the pipeline is allowed to read; never compute, convert or average them.

acceptance_criteria.given: a proposed figure whose span is not an exact substring of the source text
acceptance_criteria.then: it is dropped and logged

acceptance_criteria.given: two sources in a cluster report different values for the same quantity
acceptance_criteria.then: both are shown with sources and the cluster carries CONFLICTING_FIGURES

requirements.statement: Trends are ideas, initiatives or directions that multiple companies are pushing, tracked as a trajectory over time. A trend is CONFIRMED when at least 2 distinct verified COMPANY organizations have mentions in the last 30 days, and EMERGING with 1. Trajectory is computed deterministically from the trend ledger (FR-19) using the 7 days before the run (current) and the 7 days before that (previous): NEW if first_seen is within the current window; otherwise RISING if distinct companies increased, or stayed equal while mentions increased; FADING if distinct companies decreased, or stayed equal while mentions decreased; STEADY otherwise; DORMANT if no mentions in 30 days (hidden). hotness = 3 x distinct companies (current) + sum over distinct linked stories in the current window of w(tier) x 0.5^(age_h / 72), with w = 3 / 2 / 1 for tiers 1 / 2 / 3. Hottest topics are the top 5 CONFIRMED trends by hotness, ties broken by latest mention then trend_id.

acceptance_criteria.given: a trend whose verified mentions in 30 days all come from Shell
acceptance_criteria.then: its status is EMERGING and it is not eligible for hottest topics

acceptance_criteria.given: a trend first seen 20 days ago with 3 distinct companies in the current window and 1 in the previous
acceptance_criteria.then: it is RISING

acceptance_criteria.given: a trend first seen 3 days ago
acceptance_criteria.then: it is NEW

acceptance_criteria.given: a trend with 0 mentions in the current window and 2 companies in the previous
acceptance_criteria.then: it is FADING

acceptance_criteria.given: 2 companies in the current window and one linked tier-1 story aged 72 h
acceptance_criteria.then: it equals 3x2 + 3x0.5 = 7.5

acceptance_criteria.given: identical ledger, digest and run time
acceptance_criteria.then: statuses, trajectories, hotness and ranking are identical

requirements.rationale: Owner definition (2026-09-16): 'a trend is an idea multiple companies are pushing, essentially trajectory'.

requirements.statement: Price effects (benchmark moves beside stories) are deferred. v1 is news-only. The price module stays in the codebase disabled behind a settings flag (see NFR-9).

acceptance_criteria.given: v1 settings
acceptance_criteria.when: any page, digest or newsletter is produced
acceptance_criteria.then: no price, benchmark move or price-effect badge appears

requirements.rationale: Owner decision 2026-09-16: price data is not important yet; reading and condensing reputable news is.

requirements.statement: Render a scrollable feed of story clusters first published in the last 7 days with relevance >= threshold (default 30), newest first. relevance = round(100 x (0.6 x min(cluster_weight / 10, 1) + 0.4 x tier_score)), cluster_weight = sum over distinct sources of w(tier) x 0.5^(age_h / 72), tier_score = 1.0 / 0.66 / 0.33. Each item shows local time, title, 1-sentence extractive summary, source count and best tier, commodity chips, organizations, linked trend names, and links to every source.

acceptance_criteria.given: a cluster first published 7 days and 1 hour ago
acceptance_criteria.then: it is excluded

acceptance_criteria.given: 120 eligible clusters
acceptance_criteria.then: 25 items render and 25 more append each time the reader nears the end

acceptance_criteria.given: one tier-1 source 0 h old
a cluster with relevance 29 and threshold 30
acceptance_criteria.then: it is excluded

requirements.statement: Tabs: Newsletter (default), Analysis, Trends, All, and one per commodity (Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refined Products, Carbon Credits). Commodity tabs show that commodity's pinned analysis section, its hottest trends with trajectory badges and companies, and the filtered feed. The Trends tab lists all CONFIRMED and EMERGING trends with trajectory, companies and dated mention timeline.

acceptance_criteria.given: a cluster tagged CRUDE_OIL and REFINED_PRODUCTS
acceptance_criteria.then: it appears in both commodity tabs

acceptance_criteria.given: a commodity with no qualifying stories
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows 'No qualifying news in the last 7 days' and is not hidden

acceptance_criteria.given: the URL /#carbon-credits
acceptance_criteria.then: the Carbon Credits tab is selected

acceptance_criteria.given: a trend RISING with companies Shell, TotalEnergies and Equinor
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows a RISING badge, the three company names, and each dated mention linking to its story

requirements.statement: Feed and cluster summaries are extractive in v1: the first sentence of the best-tier source's feed summary or excerpt, never generated by an LLM API.

acceptance_criteria.given: a cluster whose best-tier excerpt is 'U.S. crude inventories fell 4.1 million barrels. Stocks at Cushing rose.'
acceptance_criteria.then: it is 'U.S. crude inventories fell 4.1 million barrels.'

requirements.statement: Freeze a weekly archive of the digest and that week's newsletters every Monday 07:00 America/Chicago; archives are immutable.

acceptance_criteria.given: the archive for 2026-W38 exists
acceptance_criteria.then: its content hash does not change

requirements.statement: Write a daily run report: sources scanned / skipped / failed with reasons, new articles, clusters, organizations tagged, digest size, flags.

acceptance_criteria.given: a completed run
acceptance_criteria.then: its totals reconcile with stored records

requirements.statement: A Claude scheduled task on the owner's Claude subscription runs daily at 07:30 America/Chicago. It reads the latest digest snapshot, may open up to 15 article links that appear in the digest to understand the stories, updates the trend ledger (FR-19), and writes a condensed newsletter issues/YYYY-MM-DD.md: title, an 'unverified, informational only' line, Hottest topics (top 5 trends: name, trajectory, companies pushing it, 2-3 sentences, links), one short section per commodity (Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refined Products, Carbon Credits) with up to 4 notable stories, Sources and Disclaimer. Target 600-900 words.

acceptance_criteria.given: the digest's data_as_of is more than 30 hours before the task starts
acceptance_criteria.then: no newsletter is written and a SKIPPED_STALE entry is appended to issues/index.json

acceptance_criteria.given: issues/2026-09-16.md already exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the task runs again that day
acceptance_criteria.then: nothing is overwritten and the task ends ALREADY_PUBLISHED

acceptance_criteria.given: a commodity with no qualifying stories in the digest
acceptance_criteria.then: its section says 'No qualifying news in the last 24 hours.'

acceptance_criteria.given: a written newsletter
acceptance_criteria.then: frontmatter records date, digest feed_sha256, data_as_of, prompt_version and articles_opened (list of URLs, at most 15)

requirements.rationale: Owner decisions 2026-09-16: the scheduled Claude task writes the newsletter; use the Claude subscription, no API.

requirements.statement: Before publishing, a deterministic validator checks newsletters and analyses. REJECT when: a URL is not in the referenced digest; the disclaimer or 'unverified' line is missing; advisory or forecast language appears; a Hottest topic names a trend that is not CONFIRMED in the validated ledger; required sections are missing. WARN (publish with a visible 'contains figures not machine-verified' note) when a number does not appear in the digest, because the author may cite figures from linked articles it opened.

acceptance_criteria.given: a newsletter linking https://evil.example/a
acceptance_criteria.then: it is REJECTED with UNSOURCED_URL and not published

acceptance_criteria.given: a newsletter citing '3.8 million barrels' where the digest has no 3.8
acceptance_criteria.then: it is PUBLISHED_WITH_WARNINGS listing UNVERIFIED_NUMBER 3.8 and the page shows the warning note

acceptance_criteria.given: a newsletter containing 'traders should buy'
acceptance_criteria.then: it is REJECTED with ADVISORY_LANGUAGE

acceptance_criteria.given: a Hottest topic for a trend whose ledger status is EMERGING
acceptance_criteria.then: it is REJECTED with TREND_NOT_CONFIRMED

acceptance_criteria.given: a rejected newsletter
acceptance_criteria.then: the Newsletter tab keeps the previous published issue and the run report shows the reasons

requirements.statement: Every scan builds a digest for the author: a JSON snapshot (validator's source of truth) and a compact Markdown digest (<= 60 KB) listing, per commodity, qualifying clusters with title, extractive summary, outlets and tiers, links, organizations and verbatim figures; candidate trend groups (topic x commodity clusters with 2+ companies); the current trend ledger with computed status, trajectory and hotness; the most active companies of the last 7 days; and the next recurring scheduled releases (EIA WPSR, EIA storage, Baker Hughes, CFTC COT). It also contains a data-only synopsis in template sentences.

acceptance_criteria.given: a day with 400 qualifying clusters
acceptance_criteria.then: it is at most 60 KB, keeping the highest-relevance clusters per commodity and stating how many were omitted

acceptance_criteria.given: the run time Tuesday 2026-09-15 12:00 CT
acceptance_criteria.then: its first entry is EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report at Wed 2026-09-16 09:30 CT

acceptance_criteria.given: identical stored data and run time
acceptance_criteria.then: both JSON snapshots are byte-identical

requirements.statement: Publish a daily analysis, 'What this means for energy traders', written by the same scheduled task from the same digest (issues/analysis/YYYY-MM-DD.md): The big picture, one section per commodity, Trend trajectories, What to watch, Data notes, Disclaimer. It explains what the collected news and trend trajectories add up to, may describe in general conditional terms how such developments are usually read, and may not forecast prices, suggest trades, or add links absent from the digest. It is shown in an Analysis tab and pinned to All and each commodity tab; if none based on data from the last 36 hours exists, pinned cards show the data-only synopsis.

acceptance_criteria.given: a submitted analysis whose links are all in its digest
acceptance_criteria.then: it is PUBLISHED and its sections are available to each tab

acceptance_criteria.given: an analysis containing 'LNG prices are likely to rise'
acceptance_criteria.then: it is REJECTED with ADVISORY_LANGUAGE

acceptance_criteria.given: the latest published analysis is based on data over 36 hours old
acceptance_criteria.then: the pinned card shows the data-only synopsis

requirements.statement: Carbon Credits is a v1 commodity with its own tab and reputable sources: official (European Commission Climate Action, ICAP, California Air Resources Board, UNFCCC) and specialist press (Carbon Brief tier 1; Carbon Herald tier 2). CDR.fyi is REFERENCE_ONLY: its terms forbid scraping and AI summarization without a commercial license, so it is shown as a static 'further reading' link in the Carbon Credits tab and never collected or summarized.

acceptance_criteria.given: the registry entry for cdr.fyi with tos_status REFERENCE_ONLY
acceptance_criteria.then: no request is made to cdr.fyi and the Carbon Credits tab shows the reference link with attribution

acceptance_criteria.given: a scan with at least one qualifying carbon story
acceptance_criteria.then: it shows the pinned analysis or synopsis, carbon trends and carbon stories

requirements.statement: The scheduled task maintains a trend ledger issues/trends.json: trends (trend_id slug, name, one-sentence thesis, commodities, first_seen) with dated mentions (date, company, story_url, action in 20 words or fewer). The ledger is append-only for mentions. The validator accepts a ledger update only if every new mention's story_url exists in a retained digest snapshot (30 days) and no existing mention was removed or changed; a mention's company is 'verified' when its name or a known alias appears in that story's digest title, excerpt or organizations. Unverified mentions are kept but excluded from trend status and trajectory.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new mention whose story_url is not in any retained digest
acceptance_criteria.then: the update is REJECTED with UNSOURCED_MENTION and the previous ledger stays live

acceptance_criteria.given: an update that deletes an existing mention
acceptance_criteria.then: it is REJECTED with LEDGER_NOT_APPEND_ONLY

acceptance_criteria.given: a mention naming 'BP' for a story whose digest organizations include BP
acceptance_criteria.then: the mention is verified

acceptance_criteria.given: a mention naming 'Aramco' where the story's digest text does not mention Aramco
acceptance_criteria.then: the update is accepted, the mention is marked UNVERIFIED_COMPANY and it does not count toward status or trajectory

requirements.statement: Host the web page on GitHub Pages with an optional custom domain from settings (CNAME, HTTPS enforced). Because the readership is small and private, every page carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">, robots.txt disallows all crawlers, and a banner states 'Private preview for a small readership. Unverified, informational only. Not investment advice.'

acceptance_criteria.given: settings site.custom_domain = 'news.example.com'
acceptance_criteria.then: a CNAME file containing news.example.com is published

acceptance_criteria.given: any rendered page
acceptance_criteria.then: the noindex meta tag and the banner are present and robots.txt contains 'Disallow: /'

requirements.statement: Cadence: the scan runs once daily at 05:00 America/Chicago; the task runs at 07:30. The page shows data-as-of and a stale banner when the last successful scan is older than 30 hours.

acceptance_criteria.given: the last successful scan finished 31 hours ago
acceptance_criteria.then: the stale banner is visible

requirements.rationale: Owner decision 2026-09-16: daily updates are enough.

requirements.statement: Determinism: the pipeline has no LLM calls; identical inputs, ledger and run time produce byte-identical digests and trend computations.

acceptance_criteria.given: the same stored data, ledger and run time
acceptance_criteria.then: digest JSON and trends output are byte-identical

requirements.statement: Cost: no API keys or per-token spend. Infrastructure is free (GitHub Actions on a public repo, GitHub Pages); the only paid items are the owner's existing Claude subscription and an optional domain. Subscription usage is bounded to one task run per day reading one compact digest (<= 60 KB) and at most 15 linked articles.

acceptance_criteria.given: the repository and workflows
acceptance_criteria.then: no Anthropic or other LLM API key, SDK call or secret is referenced

acceptance_criteria.given: a newsletter frontmatter listing 16 articles_opened
acceptance_criteria.then: it is REJECTED with READING_BUDGET_EXCEEDED

requirements.statement: Compliance and reputation: honour robots.txt and source terms; persist at most 300-character excerpts; always link to originals; never collect REFERENCE_ONLY or BLOCKED sources; the author quotes at most one short sentence per linked article; every page and newsletter carries the private-preview, unverified, not-investment-advice disclaimer.

acceptance_criteria.given: a stored article
acceptance_criteria.then: its persisted text is 300 characters or fewer

acceptance_criteria.given: any rendered page or published newsletter
acceptance_criteria.then: the disclaimer is present

requirements.statement: Traceability: every story links to its sources, every trend mention links to its story, every figure shows its source, and every trend status and trajectory can be expanded to show the mention counts behind it.

acceptance_criteria.given: a trend marked RISING
acceptance_criteria.then: the current and previous window company counts and mention lists are shown

requirements.statement: Bounded storage: raw article records kept 30 days, digests kept 30 days, the ledger kept indefinitely; no committed file over 50 MiB; data and site branches are single-commit force-pushed.

acceptance_criteria.given: a file would exceed 50 MiB
acceptance_criteria.then: the push aborts, the live site stays intact and STORAGE_LIMIT is raised

requirements.statement: Resilience: a failed scan or rejected newsletter never replaces the last good published page.

acceptance_criteria.given: the scan fails during clustering
acceptance_criteria.then: the live site still serves the previous build

requirements.statement: Least privilege: the task may only create or modify files under issues/ (newsletter, analysis, index.json, trends.json); a CI scope guard reverts task commits touching anything else.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task commit modifying config/sources.yaml
acceptance_criteria.then: it is reverted and ISSUE_SCOPE_VIOLATION is raised

requirements.statement: Growth path: price tracking, email delivery and access control can be added without restructuring. Prices sit behind settings prices.enabled (default false); access control can later move hosting behind Cloudflare Access or a private host without changing the pipeline.

acceptance_criteria.given: prices.enabled is false
acceptance_criteria.then: no request is made to any price API

glossary.definition: Official or primary publishers (agencies, regulators, intergovernmental bodies) and news organizations with a public editorial and corrections policy.
Specialist trade press and company press-release wires.
Aggregators and commentary; disabled by default.
An idea, initiative or direction that multiple companies are pushing, tracked as a trajectory over time.
NEW, RISING, STEADY, FADING or DORMANT, computed from verified company mentions in the current vs previous 7-day window.
3 x distinct companies in the current window plus tier-weighted, recency-decayed linked stories; ranks the hottest topics.
issues/trends.json, an append-only record of trends and their dated company mentions maintained by the scheduled task.
The daily JSON snapshot (source of truth) and compact Markdown version the author reads.
A source shown only as a link for further reading; never fetched or summarized (e.g. CDR.fyi).
